card.name: Nouns right after our/my/your
card.fires_on: A common noun that directly follows a possessive such as our, my or your, most often "country", also "school", "children", "treatment", "work" or "jobs". It appears in general web prose.

modes.label: our + country
modes.description: The noun "country" after "our" in civic or political writing.
modes.example: The Supreme Court heard oral arguments in Fisher v. University of Texas, a case that could potentially change the way our<< country>> handles affirmative action.

modes.label: my/your + personal noun
modes.description: A noun about the reader's own life after "my" or "your", such as children, treatment or work.
modes.example: How can I help my<< children>> stay safe online?

card.plain: It fires on the noun that comes right after "our", "my" or "your", especially "our country".
